A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 17 pages of each version, including the equations, empirical figures and Appendices A/B, support comparison. Relocated definitions, algorithms and experiments can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 Section 5 and Figure 1 report original synthetic Stackelberg-game simulations comparing Algorithm 1-OFUL with random play and, where applicable, Barycentric Explore-Then-Commit.

after.justification: V2 Section 3.5 reports original utility and regret results. Appendix A.1 also retains the earlier simulations and comparisons.

M1.justification: The utility-space reduction, OFUL and scaled logdet-FTRL instantiations, unknown-utility feature construction, and auction/persuasion adaptations remain unchanged. Algorithms 2 and 3 are relocated to the appendices without changing their procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions empirically study synthetic contextual Stackelberg games with context-dependent and context-independent follower utilities. The additional lower-dimensional simulation retains this task coverage. Auctions and persuasion remain theoretical applications.

E2.justification: V2 Figure 1 adds an optimal-policy reference to the utility comparison. Algorithm 1-OFUL, Random Baseline and the applicable Harris et al. Algorithm 3 comparison are retained in Appendix Figure 2; no existing comparator is removed.

E3.justification: V2 adds a simulation with context dimension 2, four follower types, four actions per player and 200 rounds, reporting cumulative regret alongside utility. The earlier 2,000-round experiments with context dimensions 3 and 4 retain their stated settings in Appendix A.1.

E4.justification: Neither version reports dedicated ablations, sensitivity studies, robustness tests or error analyses. V2's additional utility/regret experiment expands performance evaluation without introducing such a diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over 10 runs and show shaded uncertainty bands. V2 retains this practice for the added experiment without introducing seed information, a definition of the bands, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 Figure 1 adds utility and regret curves showing Algorithm 1-OFUL closer to the optimal policy and incurring less regret than random play in the 200-round setting. V1's two empirical plots are retained identically in v2 Figure 2. These are additional results under another configuration, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The regret bounds, discretization definitions and Appendix A/B derivations are retained. V2 explicitly describes tie-breaking as unknown but fixed and adds the offline-to-online reduction of Roughgarden and Wang to the Section 3.4 hardness argument, making limited refinements to assumptions and supporting reasoning.

C1.justification: The near-optimal regret claim, unknown-utility extension and auction/persuasion contributions remain unchanged. The introduction additionally claims a more streamlined reduction than Bernasconi et al. because it avoids a per-round application of Caratheodory's theorem.

C2.justification: V2 newly explains that discretization permits avoiding the per-round Caratheodory step and expands the explanation of compatibility with contextual bandit algorithms. The empirical interpretation, exponential-runtime limitation and lack of unknown-utility extensions for auctions and persuasion remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The general synthetic-generation descriptions and disclosure that the Harris et al. baseline's hyperparameter was tuned are retained. V2 adds no implementation procedure, concrete hyperparameter values, hardware information, runtime measurements or code/data access instructions.

R1.justification: V2 expands the Bernasconi et al. comparison, discusses principal-agent and piecewise-Lipschitz work, and distinguishes its auction setting from Flajolet and Jaillet (2017). It adds Roughgarden and Wang for hardness and removes Kamenica's 2019 survey. These focused additions refine the existing positioning; publication updates of retained references do not constitute new works.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: best-response definitions move from Section 3.4 to the preliminaries, experiments become Section 3.5 and Appendix A.1, and the expanded Bernasconi comparison moves into the introduction. Notation and citation style change throughout, and author information and acknowledgements are updated.

P2.justification: V2 adopts the ICLR layout, changing typography, headers, margins and many displayed equations into inline statements. It adds a two-panel Figure 1, relocates and rescales the original plots as Appendix Figure 2, and moves Algorithms 2 and 3 into the appendices.

improvement.justification: V2 provides a more informative empirical check through an optimal-policy comparison and explicit regret curves while preserving the original comparisons in Appendix A.1. Earlier discretization definitions and more specific research positioning also improve exposition. The gains are limited: the added evidence concerns another small synthetic configuration, and the central methods and proof derivations remain unchanged.
